name: Learning Spaces and Daisy Cubes Are Peripheral, Realizable, and Maximum-Generated
statement: Every finite learning-space graph and every daisy cube belongs to the intersection of recursively peripheral and realizable ample classes, hence is maximum-generated. Moreover $\operatorname{Cl}_{pc}(\mathsf{Learn})=\operatorname{Cl}_c(\mathsf{Learn})\subseteq\mathcal R_{\mathrm{per}}\cap\mathcal R_{\mathrm{amp}}$. A learning space on $n\ge1$ coordinates with $q$ inclusion-minimal missing consistent partial labelings has a rank-$n$ maximum parent with at most $q+2n$ auxiliaries; the zero-coordinate singleton needs none.
proof: Strict coordinate inequalities realize downsets and learning spaces on an open convex domain; a bounded perturbation and generic arrangement give the quantitative maximum parent. Recursive accessibility supplies a feasible singleton whose two sections are nested learning spaces, proving peripheral membership by induction. Learning spaces are projection closed, so the pc-closure reduces to conditioning closure; minor closure of peripheral and realizable ample classes gives the containment.
